title: This repo's relay-brief override carries the built-in Rules bullets
lead: s419 added a Rules bullet to the built-in `relay-brief.md`: the orchestrator and every role run their own shell commands in the foreground and background none. This repo customizes the template, and its override's Rules section is the old built-in text, so this repo's own `slicer ai relay-brief` output does not show the bullet.
findings_note: s419 review 2026-10-30, owner question: the repo's customized relay-brief.md override lacks the s419 no-background bullet
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing the built-in template; a general mechanism that merges built-in changes into overrides.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: This repo runs its own relays from `ai relay-brief`, so the dogfooded briefs miss the rule s419 added for every project. s412 synced its Stop bullet into the override the same way.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: - The project override of `relay-brief.md`, changed only through `slicer template set relay-brief.md --stdin` (read with `slicer template show relay-brief.md` and compare with `--default`).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: - None: this is project state, not product code. The check below is the proof.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Take the current override, add the s419 Rules bullet in the same place as the built-in, and set it with `slicer template set relay-brief.md --stdin`.
2. Keep the override's ENVIRONMENT block unchanged.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `slicer template show relay-brief.md` and `--default` differ only in the ENVIRONMENT block.
- `slicer check` passes.
